title: 60s-technical-opener-playbook-draft
summary: A compact slide + script set for SEs to open technical conversations with platform/integration teams in 60 seconds. Optimized for pilots where latency/cost/resilience are top signals. Very short, evidence-led, with 2 quick demos/fallbacks and a concise next-step CTA.
audience: Integration Architects, Platform Engineers, SREs — mid-stage discovery to quick pilot sign-off.
goal: In 60s: surface pain (latency/cost/unreliable fallbacks), establish Redwood's production guarantees, offer a low-friction pilot path (hosted -> dedicated -> private) and a technical next-step (simple perf run + canary).
context_and_problem: Field feedback: SEs often lose engineering attention in first minute. Customers ask immediate questions about latency, deterministic throughput, and failover strategies. Need a single, reproducible opener that: a) earns technical credibility; b) leads to a pilot request; c) sets expectation for instrumentation (tracing, per-route cost).
tactical_thesis: A tightly sequenced opener that combines: 1) 2 concrete numbers (latency benchmark, expected token cost delta), 2) 1 micro-diagram showing routing fallback, 3) 1 API snippet + expected response time. Close with a single CTA: "15-30min perf run + canary plan". Keep it modular so SEs can swap the model/hardware numbers.
slide_outline: Title: 60s technical opener (one-line problem + one-line value)
Why teams care: 3 bullets (latency, unit cost, reliability)
Real evidence: benchmark snapshot for a typical RAG query (p95, tokens, cost)
Fallback routing: tiny diagram (hosted -> dedicated -> private) + SLA summary
Integration leash: sample REST call, expected p50/p95, streaming vs blocking
Pilot CTA: perf run checklist + quick canary plan, who to loop in
sixty_second_scripts: Variant A (platform architect): 'Quick one — teams we work with hit 200–400ms p95 on user-facing rerank when using a dedicated pool; that cuts prompt cost ~25% vs naive single-request routing. If we run a 15min perf check against your sample prompts, we can show a tailored latency/cost tradeoff and propose a canary. Sound useful?'

Variant B (SRE focus): 'In short: we serve models with autoscaling and three-tier fallback so your app keeps serving during overloads. We can show a canary where we simulate traffic and verify failover to a quantized variant with metrics. Want to schedule a 30min run?'

Variant C (dev-first): 'We let you pin model versions, trace per-token cost, and roll back automatically on regressions. In 15 minutes we can demo a live request and instrument token-level tracing so you see cost, latency, and cache hits. Want to try?'
objection_handling_snippets: Objection: 'We manage our own infra' -> Reply: 'Great — our private deployment control plane plugs into your VPC and keeps telemetry local; we still provide the routing + runtime optimizations so you don't rewrite serving code.'
Objection: 'Quantization hurts quality' -> Reply: 'We A/B quantized variants on your eval set as part of pilot; we only recommend quant profiles where loss is within your tolerance thresholds.'

Objection: 'Costs are unpredictable' -> Reply: 'We run a sample trace to show per-route token economics and propose concrete batching/cache knobs; you'll get a projected cost curve before committing.'
quick_tech_checks: Ask for typical sequence lengths and 95th percentile tokens per request
Confirm regulatory requirement for data residency / KMS needs
Check if customer has preferred quantized model family or strict determinism needs
Get network tracer access or sample trace logs if available (helps estimate e2e latency)
evidence_snippets: Benchmark snapshot: 'RAG QPS 150, p50=120ms p95=340ms, average tokens=180, estimated token cost delta vs baseline = -23%'
Case micro-story: 'Fintech platform reduced tail latency by 40ms p95 after switching to dedicated pools + prefix caching — pilot took 2 weeks to validate.'
API example: POST /v1/generate with streaming header -> typical p50=80ms on optimized kernel (sample model: redwood-llm-8b-q4)
success_metrics: Pilot acceptance: schedule + artifact handoff within 7 days
Evidence: measurable p95 reduction or cost delta >10% vs baseline
Operational: traceable per-request cost + token-level breakdown available in console
open_questions: Do we standardize two benchmark examples (chat vs RAG) or let SEs pick numbers per account?
Should we add a short canned video (15s) showing streaming vs blocking behavior?
Who owns the "perf run" kit for SEs — solutions eng or field SREs?
Are we comfortable publishing specific model names (redwood-llm-8b-q4) in external decks?
next_steps: Create a 3-slide printable version for AE pockets (owner: Ethan)
Add a short demo recording (15s) and host on S3 for quick share
Brief Solutions Eng on pilot checklist and assert owners for perf runs
notes_to_ses: Keep it conversational. Lead with the customer's metric and close with a single ask. If they push back on numbers, pivot to a live perf show instead of debating hypotheticals.
editorial_notes: This is intentionally terse. Later iteration should include one-row cheat sheet with 'If they say X -> say Y', and a tiny diagram asset in the slide master.
